correctness.rationale: Let u=epsilon_1epsilon_2, v=epsilon_1epsilon_3, w=epsilon_1epsilon_4, independent uniform signs. A scalar quadratic chaos maps to span{u,v,w,uv,uw,vw}; its mean and cubic Walsh coefficient are zero, forcing zero sum of the four values in each parity class uvw=+/-1. Every real zero-sum four-vector satisfies sum|y|>=sqrt(2)*sqrt(sum y^2), equality exactly one positive and one negative nonzero entry. Applying to both classes with exact 8-point normalization gives ||h||_2<=2||h||_1. Equality forces one parity class zero and a signed two-point support in the other; the 12 such pairs match products (epsilon_i+s epsilon_j)(epsilon_k+t epsilon_l). n=3 has sqrt(2), n=2 has 1.
